new.title: Walk the UNESCO mound of Arslantepe
new.desc: Arslantepe is a tell on the edge of Malatya where a palace complex of the 4th millennium BC, with some of the earliest evidence of state administration, was excavated by Italian teams. It joined the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2021, and a new welcome centre opened in October 2025.
new.tip: Open daily as an archaeological site; go in the morning and allow an hour for the roofed palace and throne-room area.

new.title: See Arslantepe finds at the reopened Malatya Museum
new.desc: The Malatya Archaeology Museum was damaged in the February 2023 earthquakes and reopened after restoration and strengthening, with 1,350 square metres of indoor space on two floors. Its upper hall shows finds from Arslantepe and the Upper Euphrates basin, including Hittite-era seals.
new.tip: Visit before Arslantepe to understand the site; state museums are usually closed on Mondays.
new.q: Malatya Müzesi, Fuzuli Caddesi, Yeşilyurt, Malatya

new.title: Browse Türkiye's largest camera museum
new.desc: The Malatya Metropolitan Municipality Camera Museum, founded in 2017, displays a collection of about 2,000 cameras and thousands of accessories, billed as the largest of its kind in Türkiye.
new.tip: Plan 45 minutes; confirm it is open on the day, as municipal buildings were reorganised after the earthquakes.
new.q: Fotoğraf Makineleri Müzesi, Şehit İbrahim Tanrıverdi Sanat Sokağı, Malatya

new.title: Shop the rebuilt Bakırcılar coppersmiths bazaar
new.desc: The old Malatya bazaar district was levelled in 2023; the Bakırcılar (coppersmiths) Çarşısı was rebuilt by the ministry and formally reopened, alongside the Kuyumcular, Şire Pazarı and Mısırcılar markets in the new centre.
new.tip: Go in the afternoon when shops are open; the new bazaar is the place to buy copperware and dried apricots.
new.q: Bakırcılar Çarşısı, Şire Pazarı, Malatya Merkez, Malatya

new.title: Buy dried apricots at Hasanbey Kayısı
new.desc: Hasanbey Kayısı is a dried-apricot seller in the Şire Pazarı area on Atatürk Caddesi, run by Hasan Şahin and recommended in Malatya food writing. The Malatya area produces roughly two thirds of the world's dried apricots.
new.tip: Ask for gün kurusu (sun-dried) apricots and try pestil and iç badem; prices drop in late summer after harvest.

new.title: Order kağıt kebabı at Hacı Baba Et Lokantası
new.desc: Founded in 1942 by Hacı Mehmet Saygı, Hacı Baba is one of Malatya's oldest restaurants and a guide favourite for kağıt kebabı: lamb wrapped in thin dough and baked for hours in a stone oven.
new.tip: Order the kağıt kebabı first, then incik or kaburga; several branches exist, so confirm the address.

new.title: Eat içli köfte and analı kızlı at Ahmet Bey
new.desc: Ahmet Bey Yöresel Ev Yemekleri on Beşkonaklar Caddesi cooks home-style Malatya dishes, among them Malatya-style içli köfte (boiled, then topped with hot butter), analı kızlı and cherry-leaf dolma.
new.tip: Ring a day ahead if you want a specific Malatya dish prepared.

new.title: Try Malatya çiğ köfte at Çiğköfteci Mehmet Usta
new.desc: Çiğköfteci Mehmet Usta is a local raw-köfte shop listed among Malatya favourites; the Malatya version uses fine bulgur and spices and is served in lettuce or lavash.
new.tip: Order by the portion and have it with ayran; expect a queue at lunch.
new.q: Çiğköfteci Mehmet Usta, Malatya Merkez, Malatya

new.title: Have cheese and mince börek at Bülent Börekçilik
new.desc: Bülent Börekçilik on Altın Kayısı Bulvarı is a börek shop known for peynirli (cheese) and kıymalı (minced meat) börek, a Malatya breakfast staple.
new.tip: Go before 10:00 when the trays are fresh; pair with tea.

new.title: Stand on the Levent Valley glass terrace
new.desc: Levent Valley is a canyon in Akçadağ district, roughly 45 km from Malatya, formed by the Levent stream. A steel-framed observation terrace with a partly glass floor hangs over the gorge; a May 2026 report says the valley was preparing for the summer season.
new.tip: Best in spring and early summer; bring water, there is little shade.
new.q: Levent Vadisi Seyir Terası, Akçadağ, Malatya

new.title: Visit the Somuncu Baba complex in Darende
new.desc: The Somuncu Baba Külliyesi in Darende holds the 15th-century tomb of Hamid-i Veli, the Sufi saint known as the bread-seller (Somuncu), at the foot of Tohma Canyon, and is an important pilgrimage and tourism stop.
new.tip: Go early to avoid coach groups; dress modestly for the tomb.

new.title: See Günpınar waterfall near Darende
new.desc: Günpınar is a waterfall about 7 km from Darende where water pours down a long rock crevice, with picnic platforms, a tea garden and a restaurant beside it.
new.tip: Entry is paid; the picnic area gets busy at weekends.

new.title: Walk the Tohma Canyon trail on wooden bridges
new.desc: The Tohma Canyon is a roughly 2 km long gorge by Darende cut by the Tohma river, with wooden walkways, small waterfalls, water wheels and tea gardens along the bank beside the Somuncu Baba complex.
new.tip: Autumn colours are the best; the path is easy and takes about an hour.

new.title: Climb to Darende Castle above the Tohma
new.desc: Darende Castle (Zengibar) is a ruined fortress on the rocky hill above the town of Darende, listed among the historical sites of the district.
new.tip: Take the short climb at sunset for views over Darende and the Tohma valley.

new.title: Explore Arapgir, the Cittaslow town and its castle
new.desc: Arapgir became Malatya's first Cittaslow (slow city) in 2021. The old centre has restored mansions, the Gümrükçü Osman Paşa mosque and a hilltop castle; Roman rock tombs lie in the surroundings.
new.tip: Allow half a day and a car; Arapgir is about 150 km from Malatya.

new.title: Climb Harput Castle, the Milk Castle
new.desc: Harput Castle (Süt Kalesi) crowns the hill above old Harput; local legend says milk was mixed into its mortar during a drought. Its origins go back to the Urartian period, and the inner-castle Fetih Mescidi was reopened for worship in 2026.
new.tip: Visit in the evening for views over the plain.

new.title: See the curved minaret of Harput Ulu Cami
new.desc: Harput Ulu Cami, attributed to the Artukid ruler Fahreddin Karaarslan in the mid-12th century, is known for its leaning (curved) minaret and Artukid stonework.
new.tip: Open for worship; visit outside prayer times and dress modestly.

new.title: Visit the Arap Baba mescit and tomb in Harput
new.desc: The Arap Baba Mescidi and Türbesi complex dates to about 1279-80; the tomb houses a naturally mummified body that locals call Arap Baba, surrounded by drought legends.
new.tip: Small site; ask the caretaker before photographing.

new.title: Step into the Şefik Gül Harput culture house
new.desc: Şefik Gül Kültür Evi is a restored traditional Harput house showing the domestic life and architecture of old Harput.
new.tip: Combine with Harput castle and Ulu Cami on foot.
new.q: Şefik Gül Kültür Evi, Harput, Elazığ

new.title: Tour the new Elazığ Archaeology and Ethnography Museum
new.desc: The museum, reopened in new earthquake-resistant premises in 2026 after the 2016 attack closed the old building, shows about 2,000 pieces from the Paleolithic to the Republic, including 934 archaeological items and 522 coins.
new.tip: Allow 90 minutes; state museums are usually closed on Mondays.
new.q: Elazığ Arkeoloji ve Etnografya Müzesi, Çaydaçıra, Elazığ

new.title: Learn the city story at the Elazığ Kent Müzesi
new.desc: The Elazığ City Museum opened to visitors with exhibits on the history and urban life of Elazığ.
new.tip: A short indoor stop in the city centre.
new.q: Elazığ Kent Müzesi, Elazığ Merkez, Elazığ

new.title: Take a boat trip on Lake Hazar from Sivrice
new.desc: Lake Hazar is a deep tectonic lake near Sivrice, about 25-30 km from Elazığ, with beaches, camp sites and summer boat tours; the sunken settlement was damaged by the 2020 and 2023 earthquakes.
new.tip: Summer is the swimming and boat-tour season; the water is cold and the lake is deep.

new.title: Enter Buzluk Cave, cool in summer and warm in winter
new.desc: Buzluk Cave near Elazığ keeps a stable temperature because of underground air currents, and ice is said to survive there through summer.
new.tip: Bring a jacket in summer; check opening hours locally.

new.title: Have breakfast in a historic han at Kaburgacı Ali Usta
new.desc: Kaburgacı Ali Usta in Harput serves breakfast in a historic han with stone walls, as listed by Yemek.com.
new.tip: Arrive early on weekends.

new.title: Eat Harput köftesi and kebabı at Balakgazi Restoran
new.desc: Balakgazi Restoran offers panoramic city views and local dishes such as Harput kebabı and Harput köftesi (lean mince, fine bulgur and basil in tomato sauce).
new.tip: Ask for the Harput köftesi; sunset tables fill up.

new.title: Try Elazığ kavurma at Kömürhan Kavurma
new.desc: Kömürhan Kavurma is listed among top picks in Elazığ for kavurma, the slow-fried meat dish of the region.
new.tip: Go at lunch; serving is by weight.
new.q: Kömürhan Kavurma, Eski Malatya-Elazığ Yolu, Kumluyazı, Kale, Malatya

new.title: Order küncülü köfte at Amcanın Yeri
new.desc: Amcanın Yeri is named by the Pegasus city guide for küncülü köfte, an Elazığ köfte coated with sesame.
new.tip: Check opening times; lunch is busiest.

new.title: Taste lorik soup and Harput köfteli çorba at Elaziz Mutfağı
new.desc: Elaziz Mutfağı is recommended for traditional Elazığ dishes, notably lorik soup and Harput köfteli çorba.
new.tip: Order the two soups and a main.

new.title: See Keban Dam Lake from the dam
new.desc: Keban Dam on the Euphrates creates Türkiye's second-largest artificial lake; its shores have pine woods, picnic areas and boat services.
new.tip: Combine with a ferry across to Pertek.

new.title: Visit Palu Castle above the Murat river
new.desc: Palu Castle is a ruined hilltop fortress in Palu district, cited in Elazığ guides.
new.tip: Take a car; the road is steep.

new.title: See the Munzur Springs at Ziyaret
new.desc: The Munzur Springs (Munzur Gözeleri) at Ziyaret village in Ovacık feed the Munzur river and are sacred in Alevi culture, with birch woods around them.
new.tip: About 80 km from Tunceli; best in spring and summer.

new.title: Raft the Munzur river
new.desc: Rafting is the signature activity of Munzur Valley National Park, on a 35 km course; the R4 World Rafting Championship was held here in 2019.
new.tip: Operators start from the park entrance; season is spring to early summer.

new.title: Look over Keban Lake from Pertek Castle
new.desc: Pertek Castle, from the Mengücekid period, stands on a rock above Keban Dam Lake and can be reached by ferry across the lake.
new.tip: Combine with water sports in Pertek.

new.title: Visit the Tunceli Museum
new.desc: The Tunceli Museum has added 298 items to its collection in three years, according to Sözcü.
new.tip: Check hours locally.

new.title: Eat liver at Munzur Ciğer in Tunceli
new.desc: Munzur Ciğer is a Tunceli town-centre restaurant listed on Trip.com for liver dishes.
new.tip: Go at lunch.
new.q: 15 Temmuz Şehitler Bulvarı, Atatürk, Tunceli Merkez, Tunceli

new.title: Try Dersim dishes at Zembul Yöresel Restoran
new.desc: Zembul Yöresel Restoran Kafe in Tunceli centre serves regional dishes such as Dersim kömbe and şir.
new.tip: Ask for kömbe or şir.
new.q: Zembul Kadin Kooperatifi, Cami Sokak, Moğultay, Tunceli
